article.story:
Alexander Isak marked his return from injury with the winner as Liverpool came from behind to beat nine-man Brentford 2-1.

The Reds were misfiring as they trailed to Keane Lewis-Potter's first-half goal, but the match turned on a needless red card for Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk on the stroke of half-time.

Víctor Muñoz hauled Liverpool level after the break before Isak struck with his fifth goal of the season.

Brentford then lost Vitaly Janelt to second yellow card in stoppage time.

Swedish striker Isak had missed the previous two matches but was able start alongside Florian Wirtz and recent signing Bradley Barcola in a £350 million frontline.

Barcola, who hit a hat-trick against LASK in the Champions League on Wednesday, should have opened his Premier League account after Janelt's mistake left him with a free run on goal.

The £123m wideman attempted to chip onrushing Bees keeper Caoimhín Kelleher but made an almighty mess of his effort, tamely stabbing the ball wide to prompt a chorus of "what a waste of money" from the home fans behind the goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai's return from injury lasted just 32 minutes before the Reds midfielder was forced off with what appeared to be a recurrence of his knee problem.

Liverpool were awarded a penalty after Dango Ouattara looked for all the world like he had tripped Alexis Mac Allister in the area.

However, a VAR review showed the Bees attacker had got the slightest touch on the ball, and after a check on the monitor referee John Brooks overturned his decision.

Two minutes later Brentford took the lead when Lewis-Potter, among the smallest players on the pitch, met Igor Thiago's cross with a bullet header into the top corner.

But in stoppage time Brentford fell foul of a VAR decision, when Yarmoliuk was spotted to have aimed a 'headbutting action' towards Jérémy Jacquet as the pair grappled at a corner.

The Ukrainian's red mist earned him a red card, although Liverpool were not awarded a penalty as the ball was not in play.

Nevertheless, Liverpool made the most of their numerical advantage in the second half.

They equalised when Wirtz sent Muñoz racing down the right and the Spanish winger turned inside Lewis-Potter before arrowing a left-foot shot past Kelleher.

The winner arrived in the 70th minute when Mac Allister swung a deep cross towards the far post, Barcola headed the ball back and Isak took a touch before lashing it past Kelleher.

To rub salt in the Brentford wounds, German midfielder Janelt was sent off in stoppage time for pulling back Rio Ngumoha.
